:::{#exm-not-continuous-on}
#### A function not continuous on $\lbrack 0, 1\rbrack$

Let $f(x) = 0$ for $0 \le x < 1$ and $f(1) = 2$.
Conditions 1 and 2 of @def-continuous-on-interval hold,
but

$$
\begin{aligned}
\lim_{x \to 1^-} f(x) &= 0 \\
&\ne 2 \\
&= f(1),
\end{aligned}
$$

so condition 3 fails and $f$ is not continuous on $[0, 1]$.
@fig-not-continuous-on shows the jump at $x = 1$.

:::{#fig-not-continuous-on}

```{r}
#| label: not-continuous-on-plot
#| fig-alt: >-
#|   A horizontal segment at height 0 from x = 0 to x = 1, ending in an
#|   open circle at (1, 0), and a separate filled dot at (1, 2) above it.
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| fig-width: 4.5
segment <- tibble::tribble(
  ~x, ~y,
  0, 0,
  1, 0
)
open_end <- tibble::tibble(x = 1, y = 0)
value_at_one <- tibble::tibble(x = 1, y = 2)

segment |>
  ggplot2::ggplot() +
  ggplot2::aes(x = x, y = y) +
  ggplot2::geom_line() +
  ggplot2::geom_point(data = open_end, shape = 21, fill = "white", size = 2.5) +
  ggplot2::geom_point(data = value_at_one, size = 2.5)
```

The function with $f(x) = 0$ for $0 \le x < 1$ and $f(1) = 2$.
The open circle at $(1, 0)$ marks the [left-hand limit](calculus-derivatives.qmd#def-one-sided-limit) of $f$ at $1$, <!-- check-term-links: allow: "open circle" names the plot marker, not the geometric circle -->
and the filled dot at $(1, 2)$ is $f(1)$.
:::
